analysis: The only change in this PR is one added line in .github/workflows/ci.yml (head line 67). It adds `python3 scripts/test-provider-cluster-runtime-models.py` to the Release Integrity job, which runs on the route-selected runner with `contents: read` permissions. The step is a plain local test script invocation. It adds no new secrets, triggers, permissions, third-party actions, network access or cache keys. Provider code, attestation, encryption, the coordinator contract and the prefix-cache storage code in T-041 are unchanged, so no threat-model assets or boundaries (TB-002, TB-003, TB-007, TB-011) are affected. The workflow keeps its existing structure: actions pinned by SHA, `contents: read`, and PR-scoped concurrency. The added script's contents and its existence in the repository were not supplied, so I could not review what it executes. It runs with the job's read-only token, so this is a coverage limit rather than a finding. I found no concrete security regression, and no threat-model update is needed.
